design.issue: K-π has no onboarding: a first launch shows only the harness "No models available" warning (README.md:94-104 documents a manual /login → /accounts login → /setup-kstack sequence) and there is no /onboarding command. Research supports only Exa and Perplexity; Firecrawl cannot be configured or used.
design.root_cause: Nothing in the built-in extension factory (packages/coding-agent/src/kpi/extensions/index.ts:58-104) registers an onboarding command or a first-run session_start hook; every setup path is a separate command with its own entry (accounts/index.ts:990-1028 for /accounts login, kstack/models.ts:305-345 for /setup-kstack) and the pieces are module-private (loginAccount at accounts/index.ts:245, loginWithOfficialProvider at :198, openAuthUrl at :178; the /setup-kstack handler body is inline at kstack/models.ts:308-343; promptResearchSetup at research/setup.ts:68-84 couples the key prompts to a project-file mode write), so no caller can compose them. Research is hard-wired to two services: RESEARCH_SERVICES at research/session.ts:10, ResearchKeys :39-42, env fallbacks :60-63 and :87, mode fallback :228, endpoints.ts:13-14/32-41/103-107/136, gate.ts:134-135/145-160, setup.ts:41-51, accounts/index.ts:306-308/321, append-log.ts:79, event.schema.json:115-128, board.ts:732-738 and settings.ts:32 — adding Firecrawl requires each of those to be generalized over the service list rather than a third copy of the exa/perplexity ternaries. The revised design drops two pieces of the original that the source refutes: a "default model" step (the extension setModel at agent-session.ts:2635-2639 never persists and rejects any provider outside the harness auth snapshot, which K-π api_key pool logins never enter) and a K-π-owned writer for ~/.kpi/agent/settings.json (the harness serialises writes under a lockfile and refuses to overwrite an unparseable file; a second unlocked writer that maps parse failure to {} would be a silent, destructive catch).

evidence.note: kPi(pi) registers accounts, append-system, routing, research tools, control plane, ping, k-mode, setup-kstack, print profile, policy, renderers, status line (L58-104) — no onboarding, no first-run hook.

"auto" : "local"); notify(...)` exactly as today. Onboarding calls promptResearchKeys only, so it never writes <cwd>/.kpi/settings.json and never makes a directory trust-requiring. Slice A. New module. Exports: `ONBOARDING_COMMAND = "onboarding"`; `WELCOME_LINES: readonly string[]` (3 lines: K-π is a standalone coding-agent harness you own; a job runs a gated graph — specify → plan → implement → test → review → ship — with a plan gate and a release gate you confirm; reviewer and tester workers are separate kpi processes on the worker bus); `OnboardingDependencies { store?: AccountsStore; loginPool?: (poolId: PoolId, context: ExtensionContext) => Promise<{ poolId: PoolId; slotId: string } | undefined>; researchKeys?: (ui: ExtensionContext["ui"]) => Promise<ResearchService[]>; kstackSetup?: (context: ExtensionContext) => Promise<void> }` (defaults: new AccountsStore(), (poolId, ctx) => loginPoolInteractively(pi, poolId, ctx, { store }), promptResearchKeys, runKStackSetup); `OnboardingOutcome = { status: "completed" | "deferred"; accounts: string[]; researchServices?: ResearchService[] (present only when the research step ran); kstack: boolean }`; `export async function runOnboarding(context: ExtensionContext, dependencies: Required<OnboardingDependencies>): Promise<OnboardingOutcome>`; `export function shouldAutoOnboard(reason: SessionStartEvent["reason"], context: ExtensionContext, document: AccountsDocument): boolean`; `export function registerOnboarding(pi: ExtensionAPI, dependencies: OnboardingDependencies = {}): void`. runOnboarding steps, each via ctx.ui and each skippable: (a) notify(WELCOME_LINES.join("\n"), "info") then select("Welcome to K-π", ["Start setup", "Not now"]) — undefined or "Not now" → return { status: "deferred", accounts: [], kstack: false } with no writes. (b) Model accounts loop: read store, select("Add a model account", [...POOL_IDS.map(p => `${p}${isLocalPool(p) ? " (local server)" : ""} — ${slots} slot(s)`), "Continue"]) repeated until "Continue"/undefined; a pick calls dependencies.loginPool(poolId, context) inside try/catch — a defined result pushes `${poolId}/${slotId}` onto accounts; undefined (confirm declined) adds nothing; any thrown error → notify(`${poolId} login not completed: ${message}`, "warning") and the loop continues; one attempt per pick. (c) select("Research keys (Exa, Perplexity, Firecrawl)", ["Enter API keys", "Skip"]) → "Enter API keys" sets researchServices = await dependencies.researchKeys(context.ui); Skip leaves researchServices undefined (nothing written anywhere). (d) select("K-stack roles", ["Map roles now", "Skip"]) → dependencies.kstackSetup(context), kstack = true. (e) Summary notify: `accounts: ${accounts.join(", ") || "none"}`, `research keys: ${researchServices === undefined ? "skipped" : researchServices.join(", ") || "none saved"}`, `K-stack roles: ${kstack ? "mapped" : "skipped"}`, and the closing hint "Run /onboarding any time; /accounts and /setup-kstack edit the same files." Every step body is wrapped in try/catch that notifies `Onboarding step "<name>" failed: ${message}` ("error") and moves to the next step; runOnboarding never rejects. shouldAutoOnboard returns true only when reason === "startup" && context.mode === "tui" && context.hasUI && Object.values(document.pools).every(pool => (pool?.slots.length ?? 0) === 0) && context.modelRegistry.getAvailable().length === 0 — i.e. K-π has nothing to route and the harness has nothing either (the exact state behind the 'No models available' warning). No marker file and no settings key: 'Not now' closes the wizard for this launch only. registerOnboarding: pi.registerCommand("onboarding", { description: "Guided first-run setup: model accounts, research keys, K-stack roles", handler: (_args, ctx) => runOnboarding(ctx, resolved) }) — always runs; pi.on("session_start", async (event, ctx) => { try { if (shouldAutoOnboard(event.reason, ctx, await resolved.store.read())) await runOnboarding(ctx, resolved); } catch (error) { ctx.ui.notify(`K-π onboarding failed: ${message}`, "error"); } }) so startup never dies on it. Modelled on perplexity.ts. `export const FIRECRAWL_SEARCH_PATH = "/v2/search"`; `export const FIRECRAWL_MAX_QUERY_CHARACTERS = 500` (vendor schema maxLength); `export interface FirecrawlSearchOptions { limit?: number; baseUrl?: string; timeoutMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal; fetch?: typeof fetch }`; `export async function firecrawlSearch(query: string, key: string, options = {}): Promise<ResearchResult[]>`: fetchBounded(`${baseUrl ?? DEFAULT_FIRECRAWL_BASE_URL}${FIRECRAWL_SEARCH_PATH}`, POST, headers authorization: `Bearer ${key}` + content-type application/json, body { query: clampField(query, FIRECRAWL_MAX_QUERY_CHARACTERS), limit: Math.max(1, Math.min(MAX_RESULTS_PER_REQUEST, Math.trunc(options.limit ?? 5))), sources: [{ type: "web" }] (the v2 schema's item form is an object with `type`, verified against docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/search on 2026-09-03; the string form is not documented), timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_RESEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS } — never scrapeOptions (full page content is never requested), { service: "Firecrawl", timeoutMs, signal, fetch }). Parse JSON with asRecord; payload.success !== true → throw new ResearchHttpError(response.status, "Firecrawl") (a 200 refusal classifies as `unavailable` and cools the service — never silently empty). problems.claim: Step (f) 'Default model' persists nothing and will refuse every K-π key-only login: the extension `pi.setModel` is session-only, and its auth check reads the harness snapshot, not K-π's accounts store. The design's evidence for this step is wrong.
problems.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:2635-2639 — `setModel: async (model) => { if (!this._modelRuntime.hasConfiguredAuth(model.provider)) return false; await this.setModel(model); return true; }` calls `setModel` with no `{ persist: true }`; ModelMutationOptions at agent-session.ts:268-271 says `persist` 'Defaults to session-only'. The `setDefaultModelAndProvider` call at :1688 sits behind `if (options.persist)`. `hasConfiguredAuth` (model-runtime.ts:466-468) is `configuredProviders.has(providerId)` from the harness auth snapshot; `AccountsStore.putSlot` (store.ts:318-338) writes only accounts.json/accounts.secrets.json, never auth.json, so an api_key pool login made seconds earlier in the same wizard returns false → the design's own 'no credential for that model' warning fires. The step is dead weight (YAGNI) and its summary line 'default model' would report a value that is gone on the next launch.

problems.claim: `writeUserKpiSettings` is a second, unlocked writer for a harness-owned file and silently destroys an unparseable settings.json — the exact case the harness itself refuses to write over.
problems.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-manager.ts:251-279 — every harness write goes through `FileSettingsStorage.withLock` → `lockfile.lockSync(path)` (:224-236); `atomicWrite` (run-store.ts:168+) takes no such lock. settings-manager.ts:648-651 — `save()` returns early when `globalSettingsLoadError` is set, i.e. the harness never overwrites a file it could not parse; the design's writer reads 'missing/invalid → {}' and then `atomicWrite`s the whole document, wiping theme/defaultModel/etc. from a file with a stray comma. Harness writes are also queued asynchronously (`enqueueWrite`, :598-610), so a harness write in flight at startup (lastChangelogVersion :707-708, or anything the operator changed) can interleave with the wizard's unlocked read→rename. AGENTS.md 'Handle the failures your contracts name … Silence is a defect' and minimalist.md 'a swallowed failure is a defect' both apply: the catch that maps a corrupt file to `{}` is a silent, destructive catch.

problems.claim: The persisted marker (`kpi.onboarding {completedAt, version, status}`), the user-file writer, `KpiOnboardingMarker`, and the three-way welcome exist only to let a zero-slot install suppress the wizard forever — a product decision the design made silently, and none of the three recorded fields is ever read.
problems.evidence: Design: `shouldAutoOnboard` already requires `every pool … has zero slots`. Any successful pooled login clears that; a harness `/login` is converted into a `default` slot by `importOfficialCredentials` (accounts/index.ts:962-966, store.ts:393-420) in the accounts session_start handler, which runs before onboarding's handler (runner.ts:851-861, onboarding registered last). So the only install that ever needs 'Don't ask again' is one with no routable model at all — a non-functional K-π. `shouldAutoOnboard` checks only `onboarding === undefined`; `completedAt`, `version`, `status` are written and never consumed (minimalist.md rung 1 YAGNI, 'No speculative abstraction'). Dropping the marker deletes settings.ts change (2), the writer in (3), the schema/README/spec rows for `kpi.onboarding`, AC-31.2's marker clause and two of the three welcome options, and removes problem 2 entirely. Whether a zero-slot install should be able to silence the wizard belongs in open_questions, not in code.

problems.claim: Two unrelated changes are bundled: onboarding (new command + hook) and a third research provider (generalising 12 files over the service list). Neither depends on the other; together they touch ~20 source/test files and 12 docs and collide with four other designs in this batch.
problems.evidence: Design 'change' list: onboarding needs accounts/index.ts (export), kstack/models.ts (extract), settings.ts, onboarding.ts, index.ts, extension.test.ts. Firecrawl needs session.ts, endpoints.ts, firecrawl.ts, gate.ts, research/index.ts, setup.ts, append-log.ts, event.schema.json, board.ts, three test files. The only shared line is `promptResearchSetup` asking a third key. AGENTS.md 'Smallest correct change' and 'Rewrite unrelated files while implementing one work package' (Do not) favour two slices; fixes.md §3 already models this repo's queue as one concern per package.

problems.claim: Owning docs are not fully updated for Firecrawl: AC-28.5, AC-28.7 and AC-29.2 keep two-service wording that the new behaviour contradicts.
problems.evidence: docs/PRD.md:390 AC-28.5 'tries the other configured service' (now the next of three); :392 AC-28.7 '`exa` and `perplexity` are research credential targets, not pool ids' (firecrawl is now one too; the design only adds AC-28.8 saying 'AC-28.7 applies'); :399 AC-29.2 'With an Exa or Perplexity key … from `exa_search`, `exa_contents`, or `pplx_search`' omits `firecrawl_search`, so a firecrawl-only online run (which the design's own test 'a firecrawl key alone goes online' asserts) is not AC-covered. AGENTS.md: 'Update the owning product docs in the same package as behavior' (remediation-plan.md execution rule 8).

problems.claim: Onboarding's research step writes the project `.kpi/settings.json` of whatever cwd the first launch happens in, which makes that directory trust-requiring on the next launch — an unnamed consequence.
problems.evidence: research/setup.ts:80 `writeResearchMode(context.cwd, …)` → settings.ts:127-139 writes `<cwd>/.kpi/settings.json`. README.md:132-137: 'A project is trust-requiring when `.kpi/` contains any of `settings.json`, …' and K-π then asks 'Trust project folder?'. A first launch from `~` writes `~/.kpi/settings.json` beside `~/.kpi/agent/`. The design's risk list names the project write but not the trust prompt it causes; the PRD/README text should say it, or the research step should not write the project mode from onboarding.

problems.claim: board.ts keeps a two-service fallback string and comment after a third service is added, so an engine no-network with only a firecrawl failure that fails the name match still prints 'EXA ✕  PPLX ✕'.
problems.evidence: board.ts:736-738 — `const marks = struck.length > 0 ? struck : … "EXA ✕  PPLX ✕"`, comment 'Always show both struck marks'. The design says 'keep the … default "EXA ✕  PPLX ✕" string so operator-ui.test.ts:262-263 still holds' — preserving a test over the contract. If three services exist the default should be derived from RESEARCH_MARKS, and the test body updated with its title kept.

problems.claim: US-31 is assigned to RP-07, a closed package whose `Stories:` line does not include it; the traceability map would then show a completed package owning an unbuilt story.
problems.evidence: docs/remediation-plan.md:435-439 RP-07 'Stories: US-10–US-12, US-26', DoD all `[x]`; remediation-plan.md:9 'No incomplete remediation package remains'. scripts/generate-traceability-map.mjs:1197-1228 `usOwner` is a hand map with no cross-check, so the test passes while the map lies. The design already lists this in open_questions; it should be resolved (new package in the active queue, fixes.md `FX-##` style) before the generator is edited, not after.

required_changes: Delete step (f) (Default model) and the `setModel` dependency, or replace it with a path that actually persists — the extension `pi.setModel` is session-only and rejects any provider not in the harness auth snapshot; correct the evidence note for types.ts:1446/agent-session.ts:1688.

Remove `writeUserKpiSettings` and the `kpi.onboarding` key from ~/.kpi/agent/settings.json. If a marker survives the product decision below, store it in a K-π-owned file under the agent dir (the way accounts.json is) via the existing `atomicWrite`, and never overwrite a file that failed to parse — surface that as an error the operator sees.

Move 'may a zero-slot install suppress the first-run wizard permanently (Don't ask again)?' to open_questions. Default to the smaller design: trigger = reason 'startup' + mode 'tui' + hasUI + zero configured slots; 'Not now' = dismiss for this launch; `/onboarding` re-runs. No marker, no version/completedAt fields nothing reads.

Split the design into two slices — onboarding (accounts export, kstack extract, onboarding.ts, index.ts, extension.test.ts, docs US-31) and Firecrawl (research/*, append-log, schema, board, tests, docs AC-28.8) — so each is the smallest correct change and file ownership against anthropic-auth / board-live / plan-gate is tractable.

Update docs/PRD.md AC-28.5 ('the next configured service'), AC-28.7 (add `firecrawl`), and AC-29.2 (add 'or Firecrawl key' and `firecrawl_search`) in the same change; regenerate docs/traceability-map.json after the AC rows are bound.

Either stop onboarding from writing the project research mode (call `saveResearchKeys` only and leave mode to `/setup-kstack`), or state in README §3 / PRD US-31 that the research step writes `<cwd>/.kpi/settings.json` and that this makes the directory trust-requiring on the next launch.

Derive board.ts's default struck marks from the same RESEARCH_MARKS table instead of keeping the hard-coded 'EXA ✕  PPLX ✕' string and its 'both' comment; update the operator-ui.test.ts body, keeping the title.
